short_summary: purge runs before archive; rows destroyed unarchived
summary: Rows are purged from the database before archive() has persisted them, so any archive failure or unconfirmed call destroys account data with no copy.
failure_scenario: closeAccount(user, opts) where archive(rows, opts) throws (e.g. storage unavailable): db.purge already ran, rows are gone, archive never wrote them, data is permanently lost.

short_summary: destructive purge precedes fallible archive; no rollback
summary: The irreversible purge is performed before the fallible archive step, so a failure in archive cannot be rolled back to the pre-close state.
failure_scenario: archive(rows, opts) rejects after db.purge(rows) succeeded; caller catches the error but the account rows no longer exist and cannot be restored.

criterion_quote: Accounts must only be closed after confirmation
short_summary: confirmation check removed; unconfirmed users get closed
summary: The `user.confirmed` guard was deleted, so closeAccount now purges and archives accounts for unconfirmed users.
failure_scenario: closeAccount({id: 7, confirmed: false}, opts) previously threw 'unconfirmed'; now it proceeds to db.find, db.purge, and archive, closing an unconfirmed account.
